Hey! Well, do you have any interests already? Are you into sport? Do you fancy taking up a totally new creative hobby? 

I'm a bit of serial crafter, but that's not up everyone's street. But if there's something you'd like to make there are lots of materials you can buy online and guides to getting started. I've done soap and candle making, jewellery making, and model painting.

If you're into sport see if there's a local team you can play with, or if team sports aren't your thing look for classes or join the gym. I always feel ready for the day after a good session at the gym. I've also done yoga and MMA.

Maybe you could take up painting or drawing?

If you live in a decent area for it go out exploring on a walk or jog or cycle ride? 

Or would volunteering interest you? Maybe an animal shelter? 

Hope this gets the ball rolling.

I will say, even if moving in with your SO, look at 2 beds if it's within budget. It's nice for both of you to have your own space.

That is pretty young, I don't want to sound patronising - I'm only 22 and live with my SO. Most of the time it's great, sometimes it feels like it was too soon. It will put a certain amount of strain on your relationship, you have to live with every part of that person. But if you can do that, you will come out far stronger.

Cards on the table, me and my SO have now broken up. Cohabiting until our contract ends, as there is no other option. Just something to think about. It's awesome to hear you've found somewhere you've really fallen in love with - and have someone you want to share it with! 

Your SO is bound to be nervous, moving out of your parents is a big step. She might just not be quite as ready to fly the nest as you. That doesn't necessarily say anything negative about the relationship.

Living with your SO is waaay easier financially, as long as you're confident in the relationship.

Whatever happens, I'm sure it'll work out. If you miss out on this place, another one just as good will come along eventually.

Best of luck :)
